strategy_definition.summary: Determine the expected daily profile (London continuation vs New York reversal) by observing which session interacts with a higher timeframe PD array. Combine this context with the economic calendar to trade the expansion phase in the appropriate session killzone.

timeframes.notes: Higher timeframe bias can be established on the Daily, 4H, or 1H charts using premium/discount arrays. The session execution is monitored on the 15m chart.

other: Economic calendar alignment to confirm volatility expectations.

glossary.Classic Daily Profile: Asian range consolidation, London sweep (manipulation) creating the extreme of the day, New York retracement and continuation of London's direction, London close distribution.
glossary.New York Reversal: When Asia and London fail to tap the higher timeframe PD array, New York taps it and creates the extreme of the day, reversing the prior intraday direction.
glossary.London Close: 10 AM to 12 PM NY Local Time. Typically a time for taking profit (distribution) at a liquidity point rather than entering new positions.

custom_signals.plain_definition: Observing whether the Asian, London, or New York killzone is the one that taps the higher timeframe premium or discount array.

custom_signals.name: prior_session_expansion
custom_signals.plain_definition: A session (e.g., Asia) produces an expansion leaving a fair value gap, making it illogical to expect the subsequent session to fully retrace and sweep it.

sequence: Identify a higher timeframe (Daily, 4H, 1H) premium or discount array that aligns with the directional bias.
Check the economic calendar to anticipate which day will have the volatility to drive the expansion.
Observe the Asian session (8 PM - midnight NY Local Time). Note if it consolidates or expands.

Observe the London killzone (2 AM - 5 AM NY Local Time). If London taps the HTF array and displaces, it forms the classic profile (London extreme). Enter the retracement/continuation in London or New York.
If neither Asia nor London taps the HTF array, anticipate a New York Reversal. Wait for the New York killzone (7 AM - 10 AM NY Local Time) to tap the array, displace, and enter on the reversal.
Target an opposing HTF array or liquidity pool, and avoid taking new entries during the London Close (10 AM - 12 PM NY Local Time).

invalidation.text: If a session already has a strong expansion leaving FVGs, do not expect the next session to fully retrace and sweep its extreme.

filters.text: Do not take new continuation entries during the London Close session; it is meant for taking profit.
The economic calendar supersedes rigid session profiles; volatility is required for the intended move.
You must adapt to which session taps the HTF array; do not blindly assume London will make the high/low of the day.

entry_rule.text: Enter in the New York session during the retracement if London created the extreme, or enter in New York on the reversal if New York tapped the HTF array.
entry_rule.quote: you have to get involved right here in New York and this was a very very clean setup actually

target_rule.text: Target a higher timeframe liquidity pool or opposing premium/discount array.
target_rule.quote: it means that London clothes will take profit it will take profit at what at a liquidity Point

stop_rule.text: Place the stop loss to cover the high/low of the session that tapped the HTF array.
stop_rule.quote: that was my entry covering the high and then aiming for new lows

management.notes: Take full profit during the London Close or when the HTF target is reached.

strategy_definition.notes: The strategy emphasizes flexibility. Instead of memorizing fixed daily profiles, the trader must react to price action in real-time, observing which session interacts with the HTF PD array to determine the true profile for the day.

setup_walkthrough.what_happens: Price taps into a Daily fair value gap during the Asian session.
The Asian session expands lower immediately, leaving bearish fair value gaps.
Because Asia already displaced, London lacks the energy to fully retrace or sweep Asia. Instead, London forms a shallow retracement.
New York session begins, taps into the retracement, and provides the actual continuation setup lower.

chart_examples.presenter_commentary: The presenter stresses that trading killzones requires reaction, not rigid adherence to a template. Because the Australian Dollar is active during Asia, it caused the primary displacement. Consequently, expecting London to sweep Asia was illogical; the trader had to adapt and enter the continuation during New York.

setup_walkthrough.what_happens: Asia forms a range. London expands, sweeping both Asia lows and Asia highs, but does not reach the overhead daily fair value gap.
Because London failed to tap the HTF array, the trader anticipates New York will complete the objective.
New York session opens, rallies into the daily fair value gap, creates the high of the day, and immediately displaces lower.
A short entry is taken during the New York expansion, placing the stop loss above the newly formed NY high of the day.

chart_examples.presenter_commentary: He emphasizes that predicting a New York reversal wasn't based on Asia consolidating, but entirely on the fact that London failed to tap the daily FVG. The session that taps the HTF array dictates the true daily extreme.
